condition: Acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding — haemodynamically unstable
summary: 74-year-old man with three large maroon and fresh bloody stools, pre-syncope, HR 118 and SBP 88 after 1 L of crystalloid (shock index 1.3), Hb 8.4. BSG 2019: CT angiography first, then catheter angiography/embolisation; consider an upper GI source.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Passing large amounts of blood from the back passage
inputs.hpi: Three large maroon and fresh bloody stools in the last 4 hours; felt faint on the toilet. No haematemesis, no black stools before today. No abdominal pain. Known sigmoid diverticular disease on a colonoscopy 5 years ago. Hypertension on amlodipine. No anticoagulants, no antiplatelets, no NSAIDs. No liver disease; drinks 4 units a week.

exam.general: Pale, clammy, alert. HR 118/min, BP 88/52 after 1 L crystalloid. Capillary refill 4 s.
exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no peritonism, no masses.
exam.other: PR: fresh and maroon blood, no palpable mass.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute lower GI bleed — haemodynamically unstable
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Major acute lower GI bleed with haemodynamic instability (shock index > 1 after resuscitation). Probable diverticular source; upper GI source not yet excluded.

recommended.note: BSG 2019 defines instability as shock index > 1 after initial resuscitation.
recommended.knownGapNote: No shock-index output on web; BSG 2019 defines instability by shock index > 1.

mustInclude.note: BSG 2019: in unstable patients, CT angiography is the first investigation, followed by catheter angiography/embolisation within 60 minutes if positive. ACG 2023: CTA as the initial test in ongoing haemodynamically significant bleeding.
BSG 2019: consider an upper GI source (OGD) in unstable haematochezia, especially if CTA is negative.

mustExclude.note: No cirrhosis or varices: a variceal (upper GI) plan is wrong for this lower GI bleed, and terlipressin causes ischaemia in patients with vascular disease.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: The confirmed ICD K92.2 (GI haemorrhage, unspecified) matches the upper_gi_bleed protocol (icd10Prefixes K92) and the "Upper GI Bleed" dx-variant group; there is no lower GI bleeding protocol, so the plan is the variceal/non-variceal UGIB plan. The plan text includes "Suspected varices: terlipressin" and variceal steps for a patient without liver disease.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Remove K92 from the upper_gi_bleed protocol/dx-variant ICD prefixes (or require upper-GI words) and route lower GI bleeding to its own protocol.

guideline.name: BSG guideline — diagnosis and management of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Unstable bleeding (shock index > 1): CT angiography first; catheter angiography and embolisation if positive; OGD if no source; restrictive transfusion
guideline.citation: Oakland K, Chadwick G, East JE, et al. Diagnosis and management of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding: guidelines from the British Society of Gastroenterology. Gut. 2019;68:776–789.

guideline.name: ACG clinical guideline — management of patients with acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (update)
guideline.section: CTA as the initial diagnostic test in patients with ongoing haemodynamically significant haematochezia
guideline.citation: Sengupta N, Feuerstein JD, Jairath V, et al. Management of patients with acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding: an updated ACG guideline. Am J Gastroenterol. 2023;118:208–231.

rationale: Permutation of the low-risk case: age and haemodynamic instability. The confirmed-diagnosis ICD (K92.2, GI haemorrhage unspecified) is what the surgeon would pick for a lower GI bleed; it exercises how the web plan chooses a protocol when there is no lower-GI-bleed protocol or dx variant.
